_comment: PLACEHOLDER FIGURES - every number here was invented for the prototype. Replace wholesale before launch.

overall.label: Overall Luxury Projects Index
overall.note: The headline measure. What it costs to deliver a luxury residential scheme end to end, set at 100 in the base year and weighted across every sub-index at its share of a typical project.

labour.label: Labour Index
labour.note: Site labour: trades, supervision and site management, measured as the cost of getting a unit of work done rather than as headline wage rates.

materials.label: Materials Index
materials.note: The basket of materials prime residential work actually uses, from structure and glazing to joinery, stone and finishes, weighted by typical spend.

rawbuild.label: Raw Build Cost Index
rawbuild.note: Construction cost before anything is added on top: labour and materials in place, without preliminaries, overheads or profit.

construction.label: Construction Cost Index
construction.note: The contractor's full figure for building the scheme, being raw build cost plus preliminaries, overheads and profit.

fees.label: Professional Fees Index
fees.note: Architects, engineers, project managers, cost consultants and specialist designers, tracked against construction cost.

ohp.label: Contractors OH&Ps Index
ohp.note: The overhead and profit a contractor adds to the raw build cost, tracked as a percentage of it.

prelims.label: Contractors Preliminaries Index
prelims.note: Running the site rather than building on it: welfare, scaffolding, plant, site management, insurances and programme costs.

landscaping.label: Landscaping Index
landscaping.note: Everything outside the building line: hard and soft landscaping, garden structures, drainage, external lighting and planting.

ffe.label: FF&E Index
ffe.note: Loose furniture, fittings and equipment specified for the finished house. Anything built in sits under construction cost instead.

allin.label: All-in Project Cost Index
allin.note: The whole bill a client carries: construction, professional fees, FF&E, landscaping, statutory costs and contingency.
